transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-02
Time: 11:00 AM PT / 2:00 PM ET
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Diego (CSM); Maya (NexusCare Head of Product), Ethan (ML Eng), Lucille (Security), Tom (SRE), Priya (Data Analyst)
Shared artifacts: pilot-metrics.xlsx (gdrive link), prompt-ensemble-v2.csv (gdrive link), security-summary.pdf (redwood link)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Reviewed this week's scorecard: small uplift on intent recall but spike in hallucination on long-context prompts.
- Ran prompt-ensemble A/B: ensemble reduced false positives by ~6% but increased latency in hosted mode.
- Security checkpoint: customer requested audit log retention details and KMS options for private deployments.
- Agreed next steps: pricing + KV-cache benchmark, share 200 edge-case prompts, security follow-up.

Topics discussed: 1) ensemble scoring and prompt sets 2) regression examples and bisect 3) hosting vs dedicated perf tradeoffs 4) security/KMS/audit logs 5) rollout plan and next demo

[00:00] Samira: okay, hi everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off. Uh quick roll call, I think we have uh Maya, Ethan, Lucille?
[00:08] Maya: yep hi all, thanks, morning, afternoon, yes we're here.
[00:12] Jordan: morning, Jordan from Redwood, I'll be driving the quality bits.
[00:16] Diego: and Diego from success, quick note I'll follow-up on scheduling for the canary.
[00:22] Priya: hey, Priya here, will be feeding the prompt set updates.
[00:26] Tom: Tom - SRE - on for infra constraints.

[02:05] Samira: ok, so agenda, quick recap of last week's pilot metrics, then Jordan will walk the regression examples and the prompt ensemble results, Lucille will call out security asks, and then we do action items. Anything to add?
[02:17] Maya: no that sounds right. Really want to focus on those hallucination spikes we saw in long doc summarization.

[05:12] Jordan: alright, jumping in - on the scorecard we saw intent recall improved from 91 to 94 percent for our primary intents using the ensemble. But we also saw hallucination rate for long-context (>3k tokens) go from 2.1 to 4.8 percent in hosted runs. Part of that is our ensemble weighting favoring the more creative variant - so it's a precision/recall tradeoff.
[05:41] Ethan: can you repeat the hosted/dedicated numbers? we wanna see if dedicated hardware flips that.
[05:46] Jordan: sure, on the hosted tests latency p95 went from 420ms to 560ms with the ensemble, cpu and batching changes; on a dedicated small pool the p95 was 380ms with ensemble and hallucination rate dropped to 3.1 percent — so dedicated helps but not magically. Also caching behavior differs - our prefix cache (K V cache) was more effective on the dedicated nodes because of longer-lived kernels, hmm sorry K V cash in transcript sometimes reads weird.
[06:18] Tom: is that with the same sequence length distribution? I'm concerned the customer test had more 4k+ examples.
[06:25] Jordan: good call - the ensemble run had a heavier tail, we can reweight to keep recall while lowering hallucination; the ablation suggested the creativity head contributes most to FP.

[10:02] Maya: show us a few regression examples, please, the ones that failed after last week's prompt update.
[10:10] Jordan: yep, pulling up prompt-ensemble-v2.csv; example one, question about patient med history, earlier variant correctly refused based on policy, the ensemble sometimes produced a partial answer with hallucinated meds. Timestamped logs attached in gdrive.
[10:34] Priya: that one looks like it's sensitive because the ground truth should be refusal. We need guardrails tightened for medical entities.
[10:42] Lucille: on that note, we need the exact audit event schema - who can access refusal events, redaction rules, retention. Also KMS integration for private deploy is a must for our compliance.
[10:56] Samira: totally - Diego, do you want to comment on KMS options?
[11:02] Diego: yes, we support customer-managed KMS via our private plane for Private Deployment — sorry private plane not plane — private control plane. We can integrate with AWS KMS or GCP CMEK, and we log key usage in audit logs. There is a slight perf delta for envelope decryption, usually +10-20ms per request.
[11:28] Lucille: that delta is acceptable, but we need to see the SOC2 scope and retention policy.
[11:34] Samira: we'll share security-summary.pdf after the call and tag the SOC2 section.

[15:05] Jordan: back to regression triage - we ran an ensemble ablation yesterday: removing creative head reduced hallucination by ~2.8 points but recall dropped by ~2 points. A compromise is to selectively apply the creative head only on low-risk intents and fallback to conservative variant on high-risk medical prompts. We can do that routing in the prompt router.
[15:30] Ethan: can that be done client-side via a heuristic? we prefer to keep routing decisions deterministically in our service.
[15:36] Jordan: yes you can run a small preclassifier to tag risk level, or use our rule-based router at the API layer. Both are possible; we'll demo the router in next week's session.

[19:50] Priya: on prompt set, I uploaded 200 new edge-case prompts to the shared folder this morning, flagged as high-risk. Some of those are long transcripts with obfuscated names which triggered hallucination.
[20:02] Jordan: perfect, we'll fold those into the scoring dataset and run a focused bisect to find which prompt templates cause the shift.

[23:14] Tom: infra question - if we go dedicated, what's the expected autoscaling behavior for peak loads? we can't accept cold starts over 1s.
[23:24] Diego: our dedicated pools keep a warm set; autoscaling can be configured with burst capacity and prewarmed nodes. Cold-starts are typically <200ms for our models if KV cache warm, but worst-case first GPU init can be higher; we recommend a small base capacity for predictable latency.
[23:41] Tom: ok we'll test with our traffic replay to validate.

[27:55] Maya: about cost - the ensemble seems to add tokens/compute. Can you share the hosted vs dedicated cost delta with our current traffic profile?
[28:02] Samira: yes i'll share a breakdown, but rough numbers: hosted ensemble ~1.4x compute units vs baseline; dedicated with batching + KV cache tuning we expect 1.15x. I'll convert to $ per 1M tokens in a spreadsheet and send.
[28:17] Ethan: could quantization help without hurting medical accuracy?
[28:21] Jordan: 4-bit quantization yields good perf, but for safety-sensitive prompts we recommend FP16 on dedicated. We can run a quick quality check on the quantized variant with your 200 edge prompts.

[32:40] Lucille: on logging - we need redaction controls. Historically our privacy team wants PII redacted at ingestion and certain events masked in logs. Is that supported?
[32:50] Diego: yes, we have pre-ingest transformers to scrub PII and redaction rules that can be applied to logs; we stop logging raw prompts optionally for private deployments. There is an operational tradeoff for debugging.

[36:01] Jordan: quick demo of ensemble ablation results - showing waterfall chart: creative head contributes +5 recall on small intents but +3.5 hallucination on long-context. Visual attached in deck link.
[36:23] Maya: can we get the raw examples where hallucination occurred? need to share with clinical safety team.
[36:30] Jordan: yes, those are in the gdrive with timestamps and model outputs. We'll mark the severity by false-positive vs hallucination.

[40:12] Samira: ok recap: Jordan to run KV-cache bench and ensemble ablation on dedicated nodes and share logs; Samira to share cost sheet; customer to drop edge prompts; Lucille to send SOC2 scope Qs. Anything missing?
[40:25] Priya: one ask - can we get per-route latency and token cost broken down in the console? it's tricky to map to our product routes.
[40:33] Diego: yes per-route metrics exist, Diego will share a query for the console that maps route->model->cost.

[44:01] Ethan: small nit - on the prefix caching behavior, is there a TTL we can tune? we saw cache thrash with many unique conversations.
[44:09] Jordan: yes TTL and size limits tunable; for your workload a sliding-window TTL of 12 hours may be better than evict-on-idle. We'll recommend settings after running the replay.

[48:30] Lucille: security follow-up - please also provide contact for your compliance engineer; we might want a short conference with our legal.
[48:38] Samira: I'll introduce you to Priyanka Kumar from our security team.

[50:00] Diego: ok final logistics - next sync same time next week?
[50:06] Maya: yes same time works.
[50:10] Samira: great, we'll send calendar invite and notes. Thanks everyone.

[51:12] Maya: thanks all, bye.
[51:15] Jordan: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription artifacts: occasional mis-hear of "KV cache" as "K V cash", "private plane" -> "private plane" (should be "private control plane"), speaker overlap near 10:10 produced garbled tokens.
